label: Early copy-phase steps (outputting original tokens 2-5), boosted by j/p/g
explanation: Fires almost only in the copy phase (99.8% of activation mass). It is silent on the delimiter step and on the first copy step, and almost never fires during the original phase. Firing rate peaks when the model outputs original token 3 (52% of those steps active) and falls off on both sides: 30% at recall_idx 2, 38% at 4, 19% at 5, about 10% later, 1.5% at recall_idx 1. Within that window, token identity modulates both whether it fires and how strongly. The largest activations come when input j, p or g is followed by output p or g (e.g. input j at recall_idx 2-3 reaches 0.9-1.0 of max); out_tok g/p have about 5x lift. Restricting the predicate to j/p/g raises precision to about 0.6-0.67 but drops recall below 0.5. The predicate captures 93% of the activation mass but only about 36% of predicted steps are active, so the remaining selectivity (token-dependent) is not captured.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the token being output (most: g, p, b, t, i, r; least: d, x, v, c) and the current input token, by phase (copy phase: j, p, g, 0; input phase: x, w, d, n; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=2, L=9 & t=12.
